title: A held-out validation protocol for shape-generalization claims in kernel dispatch, with positive and negative evidence on GB10
abstract: Dispatch rules for GPU kernels - which variant runs at which input shape, and when to trust it - are claims about shape space; validating them on the shapes they were tuned on is circular. We present a held-out validation protocol for such claims, stated as five reporting requirements, and apply it on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_120) over reduction, conv-as-gemm and layer-normalization families. Under a validate-then-time correctness contract (benchmark 1e-4 rule, per-arm declared precision), no budgeted autotune arm (b<=8) matches a zero-probe family-local gate's total time including probes on either family (preregistered rule); cold-start parity arises only on the minority of shapes with any positive crossover, at ~100-600 revisits, and the conv-as-gemm cold-start gap rests on a single admissible hand row. At one-shot delivery the correctness-gated gate emits torch on 53/56 conv rows; against torch.compile its paired delivery-regret advantage is +11.9/+12.1/+10.3 percent (t 2.44/1.64/1.60) across the grid-repaired families, with reference-realization stability carried as scenario columns (fp64 anchor: delivered arm changes on 21/56 rows). Elementwise bandwidth is repeatable in (bytes per thread, resident waves) to 0.55 percent median residual, against 36 percent for bytes per thread alone. A trained admission guard transfers rank-ordering across op families (AUC 0.80 repaired) but not its calibrated operating point (coverage 0.167, precision 0.67, against a 0.90 target); the failure localizes to family-constant score components. Scripts, frozen rules, preregistrations and byte-identical result files are released; single-accelerator scope is stated explicitly.
change_summary: Repair of all four findings of rejection O4hnCxiPVenpDr4A, each verified against retained records before this revision. (V1/R1) The 4 mis-gridded held-out rows rerun on the frozen (N,H,C) grids (r42_gridfix, 4/4 rows); corrected-oracle analysis regenerated on the 56-row union (r42_analysis): gate regret 0 on every row, paired delivery d_i +11.87/+12.08/+10.30% (t 2.44/1.64/1.60) replaces the inadmissible +56.8/+32.1 pp comparison, and the 'direction survives' claim is dropped. (V2/R2) Probe economics recomputed under the contract: validate-then-time rerun of the unchanged m3 grids/seed/budgets (m3_r42, 96 rows, selection over contract-passing arms, replacement budgeted-autotune probes); the preregistered gate-wins rule is met on both families; cold-start deltas restated (reduction +0.0040 SE 0.0021; conv +0.0034 SE 0.0034, one admissible row); break-even medians reported with finite-row counts; economics scoped to the warm measured accounting. (V3) Oracle/summary consistency: corrected oracle min(passing hand, torch), gate rule stated without min-guard, all regrets on the corrected basis. (V4/R4) Byte-identical packaging (release sha256 == repository sha256, MANIFEST verified at build), runner paths de-absolutized, previously absent w3_conv_gemm.json/calibration/a1 artifacts added, ref_absmax semantics documented as magnitudes, rider artifacts cited for all reference-error claims. (R3) Evaluation population defined as designed grids with a per-experiment requirement-map table; 'falsifiable only with' softened to sufficient reporting discipline; claims carry reference-realization scenario columns (fp64-anchor rider, ieee rung, declared-null bootstrap).
